summary.text: The Space Race was a 20th-century competition between the United States and the Soviet Union to achieve superior spaceflight capability.
It grew out of the missile-based nuclear arms race after World War II, because spaceflight skill was seen as necessary for national security.
It produced pioneering satellites, robotic landers and human spaceflight, and ultimately reached the Moon.

facts.label: Kennedy's goal
facts.value: Land a man on the Moon by decade's end

items.prompt: Why did governments treat the ability to launch things into orbit as a matter of national security?

options.label: Satellites could earn money from television
Spaceflight skill backed missiles and reconnaissance
Rockets were needed to carry troops overseas
Orbit was needed to claim land on the Moon

items.explain: Spaceflight achievement was seen as necessary for national security, particularly for intercontinental ballistic missile and satellite reconnaissance capability.

items.prompt: What earlier development made launching the first satellites possible?

options.label: Large ground telescopes
Radio broadcasting networks
Fast jet airliners
Ballistic missile capabilities

items.explain: The launching of satellites was enabled by developments in ballistic missile capabilities since the end of World War II.

items.prompt: In April 1961 the Soviet Union sent the first human into space. How did the US president respond?

options.label: He asked Congress to commit to landing a man on the Moon
He proposed handing spaceflight over to a joint program
He cancelled American satellite launches to save money
He told Congress to match Soviet orbits only

items.explain: Gagarin's flight led Kennedy to raise the stakes by asking Congress to commit to landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely before the decade ended.

items.prompt: Why did the launch of Sputnik 1 cause a "crisis" in the West?

options.label: It crashed and showed Soviet rockets could not be trusted
It was an American satellite that failed on the launch pad
The USSR had achieved the first successful satellite launch
It showed that satellites could carry people to the Moon

items.explain: The competition gained Western public attention when the USSR achieved the first successful satellite launch.

items.prompt: In 1975 a US astronaut crew and a Soviet cosmonaut crew met in Earth orbit. What does this say about how the Space Race ended?

options.label: Cooperation gradually replaced the competition
The US won outright and the USSR quit space
The USSR beat the US to the Moon that year
It ended suddenly when the first station launched

items.explain: The Apollo-Soyuz rendezvous was seen as a final act of the race by many, but the competition was only gradually replaced with cooperation.

items.prompt: The Soviet crewed lunar programme never landed anyone on the Moon. What did the USSR do with that effort?

options.label: It handed the rocket to the US in return for Apollo data
It restarted the programme after the Shuttle-Mir deal
It switched to building another Saturn V-class lander
It canceled it to focus on Salyut and Venus and Mars landings

items.explain: The USSR eventually canceled its N1-based lunar plan to concentrate on Salyut, the first space station program, and the first landings on Venus and Mars.
